question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}83 & ≡8\cdot 10+3\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡8\cdot 0+3\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 96 & ≡9\cdot 10+6\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡9\cdot 0+6\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}83\cdot 96 & ≡3\cdot 6\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡18\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡10+8\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+8\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
83\cdot 96\text{ mod }10=8.
$$
